I've been farming these 15 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. My old man taught me, and I went to middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and understand what the extension fellow says, but at the end of the day I do what works on my own land.

I keep 10 mu in wheat-maize rotation and 5 mu in cotton. The wheat went in last October — I rotary tilled and sowed Jimai 22, about 15 kg per mu. At planting I put down one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu, the 18-20-5 kind, that's 50 kg. When it greens up in March I'll topdress with urea, about half a bag per mu, 25 kg. I irrigate three times: once around New Year if the winter is dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Three sprays too — herbicide in spring, then fungicide when I see rust, then insecticide for aphids. Last year I got about 450 kg per mu and I expect the same if the rain comes right.

For summer maize, the day the wheat comes off in early June I plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, about 2.5 kg per mu. No time to plough deep — I no-till or do one quick rotary pass if the straw is thick. I put compound in the furrow at planting, about 40 kg per mu of the high-nitrogen type, 26-8-10. At big flare stage I spread urea, about 15 kg per mu. Two irrigations — one if it's dry at sowing, one at the critical grain-filling stage. Two pesticide sprays, herbicide and insecticide. I figure on 500 kg per mu.

The cotton takes the other 5 mu. I plant Guoxinmian, the improved Bt variety, in late April after rotary tilling. Basal fertilizer is compound, about 40 kg per mu of 16-16-16. When flowering starts I topdress with urea, about 20 kg per mu. Cotton needs water at flowering and boll stage, so I irrigate twice. But cotton needs more medicine — I spray five times total for bollworms, leaf diseases, and growth control. Last year the cotton gave me 250 kg per mu of seed cotton, and I'll be happy with that again.

Why these amounts? Because that's what I've done for years and it's what the successful farmers around me do. Two years ago I tried saving 10 kg of urea per mu on one wheat plot to cut costs, and the yield dropped by nearly 50 kg per mu. I lost more money than I saved. Never again. Urea is over 100 yuan per bag now, fertilizer is my biggest expense, but a bad harvest is a disaster and wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. With my son working in the factory in Handan, I have some cash coming in, but I still watch every yuan. I keep the cotton to only 5 mu because my wife and I are getting older, and with my son only home for the busy seasons, I don't have the labor for more. The wheat-maize gives me steady grain and income, the cotton gives cash but needs more hands. This is the balance that keeps my family going.
